items.title: ACT data reveals which schools will face the biggest budget cuts
paras: Majura Primary School in Watson will see its funding drop by 13.4 per cent from its projected spend in 2026. ( ABC News: Mark Moore )
More than 40 ACT public schools will see a reduction in their budgets for next year, compared with their projected actual spending this year.
Fifty schools will see an increase in funding compared to their 2026 projected spending.
The ACT government has bowed to pressure to release information on previous school budgets.
Forty-one ACT public schools will have their total budgets cut in 2027, with five schools facing reductions of more than 10 per cent, new figures show.
The ACT government today released public school budgets across four years, ahead of changes to the way funding is distributed next year.
The government has been under pressure to be more transparent after it last week announced 18 schools would face budget cuts of more than 5 per cent .
The government had previously refused to say which schools were facing cuts, calling it a "psychosocial risk" for school staff.

"A little bit of time has passed; that additional information isn't going to create such a headache for our principals and school leaders because they've already been able to have those conversations with their communities about what 2027 is going to look like," ACT Education Minister Rachel Stephen-Smith said.
In total, 41 out of the ACT's 91 public schools will see a reduction in their budgets for next year, compared with their projected actual spending this year.
Fifty schools will see an increase in funding compared to their 2026 projected spending, including 22 schools which will see an increase of more than 5 per cent.
Education Minister Rachel Stephen-Smith said 2027 budgets would be confirmed when enrolments were known. ( ABC News: Luke Stephenson )
In 2026, schools were given a one-off funding injection to manage budgets while a review into school resourcing was being carried out.
The newly released data shows that compared to their 2025 budgets, all schools, except for one, will see a rise in their overall 2027 budgets.
That outlier is Wanniassa Hills Primary, although its enrolment numbers also fell by around 12 per cent.
The government has previously refused to say which schools were facing cuts. ( ABC News: Adam Shirley )
The government said 2027 budgets were calculated based on current enrolments, with an aim to make distribution of public funds more equitable.

"If the overall number of public-school enrolments increases, that obviously results in an increased level of funding coming into the public education system because it is based on the number of students," Ms Stephen-Smith said.
"If enrolments change between schools, that's where we have been really clear that budgets won't be finalised until March or April."

items.title: Grocer says he was threatened with fine over Scrap the Tax sign
paras: Dean Lamb takes down a Scrap the Tax sign after a notice from the council. ( Supplied: Watts Fresh/Facebook )
A Kyneton business owner says he was threatened with a $2,900 fine by his local council if he did not reduce the number of political signs displayed on his property.
Dean Lamb disputes the council's assessment that the signs constitute election advertising.
A council spokesperson says it deems any sign with a political message as falling under the state's planning provision laws.
A central Victorian business owner says he was threatened with a $2,900 fine by his local council over the number of political signs displayed outside his store.
Kyneton greengrocer Dean Lamb says he was given 48 hours by Macedon Ranges Shire Council to reduce the number of signs displayed outside his store to one, or face "enforcement action".

A letter sent to Mr Lamb, seen by the ABC, said a roadside inspection had "found multiple signs relating to the upcoming election" on his property, exceeding the number permitted without a planning permit.

Mr Lamb, who owns Watts Fresh in the central Victorian electorate of Macedon, had been displaying two Scrap the Tax signs protesting the state government's Emergency Services and Volunteers Fund (ESVF) levy, as well as a sign supporting Liberal candidate Kate Kendall.
Dean Lamb says his Scrap the Tax signs are a protest against the government policy. ( Supplied: Dean Lamb )
He said the protest signs had been displayed outside his business for at least six months before he was contacted by the council earlier this month.
The levy, which Mr Lamb said had added to the cost of doing business, has been a controversial issue, particularly in regional Victoria and has triggered major protests.
Earlier this month, Victorian Labor vowed to permanently freeze the contentious ESVF levy charged on farmland if it won re-election.
Mr Lamb said he disputed the council's assessment that the Scrap the Tax signs were election advertising.
"Initially the contact from council said you can't have more than one electoral sign, and I said, 'Well, we have only got one electoral sign,'" he said.
The Labor government says it would permanently freeze the emergency services tax rate imposed on farmland. ( Supplied: Dean Lamb )

Mr Lamb said he had been contacted by people from other businesses that had received similar letters from council, and said he had since moved one of his signs onto a footpath, where he already held a permit.
"They have sort of cracked down a little bit … I'm not a big fan of signs all over the countryside either, but I think there also is a point where you need to stand your ground," he said.
"If you think you've got a valid reason to protest, then you should exercise that right and do everything you can to make sure that message gets across."
In a statement, Macedon Ranges Shire Council planning director Rebecca Stockfeld said the council did not determine whether a sign was political based on what it promoted.
"The planning scheme does not specifically define 'political signage', so council applies the ordinary meaning of the term," she said.
"In practical terms, this includes signage that supports, opposes or comments on political candidates, parties, campaigns or political issues and the like."
She said the council had not sought advice from the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) on the matter.

While the VEC regulates the authorisation and certain aspects of the content of electoral advertising, the number, placement or size of signs outside of polling centres falls under local councils' remit.
Zoe Daniel at a polling booth on election day in 2022. ( ABC News: Kristian Silva )

In 2022, those provisions were put to the test in Victoria's Supreme Court after the campaign director for former ABC journalist and independent federal candidate Zoe Daniel took legal action against Bayside City Council.
The council had threatened enforcement action against residents displaying signs in support of Ms Daniel's bid for the Melbourne seat of Goldstein before the federal election had been called.
The court found residents were entitled to display the signs before an election was formally called, provided they met the conditions of the planning permit exemption.
Victoria's planning provisions allow for one single election sign on private property. ( ABC News: Nate Woodall )
Under Victoria's planning provisions, a single sign up to 5 metres large publicising a local political event can be displayed on a property without a planning permit.
A political sign can be displayed for no longer than three months in total, and must be removed within 14 days after an election.
For the upcoming election, the latest date signs can be displayed is December 12.

items.title: Using AI to hunt for Black Friday bargains? That ‘great deal’ might not exist
paras: The Conversation , CC BY-SA Using AI to hunt for Black Friday bargains? That ‘great deal’ might not exist Published: November 25, 2026 9:08pm EST To get the most out of Black Friday sales, a bit of research is always useful. Ideally, this involves working out what you might want to buy – and checking prices – before sales begin.
Once the sales are under way, comparing prices, delivery costs and delivery times at different stores can feel onerous and time-consuming, especially if you’re worried you might miss out on a deal.
To streamline their search for a bargain, some shoppers are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) tools to do the research for them.
Can AI really help you snag a deal? The answer is yes, maybe. But there are reasons to proceed carefully.
AI is being used to take the legwork out of all sorts of tasks. It makes sense consumers across the world are increasingly putting it to work as a shopping companion .

Say you’re looking for a new coffee machine or laptop this Black Friday. Rather than trawl through dozens of different sites yourself, you might ask a tool such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini to search the web for you and prepare a spreadsheet with a list of options.
A recent survey by the Australian Retail Council and market research firm Roy Morgan found this Black Friday, one in four respondents were planning to use an AI chatbot for research.
Among this group, 72% said it would be their first time doing so. If you fall into this category, there are a few things to be aware of as you check any recommendations.
Hallucination is a well-known feature of generative AI tools. In the context of shopping with AI, this means some products, prices and stores may be entirely made up or misinterpreted.
A related concern is whether AI tools can reliably distinguish between genuine online stores and the fake or “ ghost stores ” that spring up online during sales periods.
Many AI tools, including the free and low-cost versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google Search’s AI Overview and AI Mode , have already started rolling out advertising.
Both OpenAI and Google say advertisements shown to users are clearly labelled. But depending on your settings, the ads you see may be informed by your previous conversations with these tools.
Other generative AI tools don’t have ads. Anthropic, for example, has pledged to keep Claude ad-free. And Google’s Gemini app remains free of advertising , at least for now.
Even if you decide not to use AI this Black Friday, it could still shape the deals you see. Some retailers are reportedly already using AI to guide their discounting strategies .
This includes using sophisticated models and past sales data to work out the smallest discount they need to offer to sell a product.
Another potential headwind for shoppers is the use of AI by retailers to personalise prices to the amount a consumer is likely to be prepared to pay, sometimes called “ surveillance pricing ”.
Currently, this is not explicitly against the law unless the surveillance pricing involves discrimination based on protected characteristics such as race, sex or disability.
Read more: AI is using your data to set personalised prices online. It could seriously backfire

By Black Friday next year, new tools which go beyond simple research may be more commonplace: AI shopping agents. These tools can find stores selling what you’re looking for, compare prices and then complete the purchase on your behalf.
For example, Meta’s Muse agent, which launched in Australia last week , integrates with existing social media accounts and can complete tasks on your behalf.

Other tech companies are also venturing into the space. OpenAI recently launched its Dots agent, and Google’s offerings include Agentic Checkout and Gemini Tasks . Amazon offers its own shopping agent but blocks other third-party agents from accessing its site.
Developers such as Meta say they are building in protections to prevent consumer AI agents “going rogue” and overstepping their authority or spending instructions.

But even with safeguards in place, other risks could be amplified. AI agents rely on “context” to execute the purchases their consumers are likely to prefer. Essentially, this means information about your previous interactions is used to predict what you might want in the future.

More broadly, there is the risk AI tools may not be working in shoppers’ best interests. An OECD paper this month warned commercial partnerships could shape which products and prices AI tools recommend, in ways that may not be understood by shoppers.
The federal government has flagged new laws may be needed to respond to the rise of AI shopping agents, including to guard against manipulation or exploitative personalised pricing.
So, what’s the advice? By all means, use AI to find a Black Friday bargain, if you choose. But be sceptical. Treat its recommendations as just one piece of information.
It is worth checking the policies of your preferred AI tool to see if you can turn off its memory of earlier chats.
You may also be able to limit advertising and prevent your prompts from being used for training.
Ultimately, getting the best deal still means weighing up your options, sticking to a budget and thinking about whether you really need what’s on sale.

items.title: These seven jobs don’t exist. By 2050, they’ll have millions of workers
paras: Advertisement Business Workplace Jobs Opinion These seven jobs don’t exist. By 2050, they’ll have millions of workers Tim Duggan Work columnist November 26, 2026 — 12:45pm November 26, 2026 — 12:45pm
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A The future is famously difficult to predict, just ask anyone who is certain they’ll get rich by picking individual shares, or someone who guesses what the weather will be like too far in advance.

But while specifics are difficult to pin down, there are global megatrends sweeping through society that show the directions we’re heading in. Big shifts in technology, health breakthroughs and wellbeing are fundamentally changing how we work and creating new jobs that we haven’t even thought of yet.

What are some of the jobs that don’t exist today, but will have millions of workers by 2050? Sam Mooy The scale of these predictions can be murky to quantify, with high percentages often thrown around. One report from Dell in 2017, which cited experts who attended a workshop, said that “85 per cent of the jobs of 2030 haven’t been invented yet.” We’re now a few years from that deadline and, well, we’re still doing many of the same jobs that we were a decade ago.

But when you look back at a broader swathe of history, the shifts become clearer. An MIT economist reviewed 80 years of census records and found that around 60 per cent of jobs we do today weren’t being done in the 1940s.
With everything seemingly speeding up, what are some of the jobs that don’t exist today, but will have millions of workers by 2050? Here are seven examples:

1. AI manager. We’re already seeing the first wave of this new way of working, with people setting up “AI agents” to work in the background on tasks they give them. As this naturally progresses, there will be entire roles created for leaders who manage broad teams of AI workers that will become only more sophisticated.

2. Electronic auditor. How much do you trust what comes from the AI responses that you get? In the future, you’ll likely have employees whose job is to determine if the output is correct and verified. In the same way that financial auditors grew from the need to double-check information, this role certifies facts, as well as what is human or machine generated.

3. Workflow redesigner. This is one direction that HR is heading, where a professional is brought in to understand the workflows of a job, department or company, and pulls apart the tasks, skills and processes to achieve it. As workplaces get more complicated, this profession will help to constantly redesign them to try to keep up.

4. Longevity coaches. Health is another major area that’s rapidly advancing alongside our understanding of how to live longer. We will need coaches to help us navigate everything from lengthened careers (50 years of working, anyone?) to keeping our muscles and organs working overtime and even how to maintain relationships for longer than we ever have before.

5. Care technologist. The older we live, the more help we will need setting up and maintaining technology in our homes. This role will combine the skills of a tradie with an aged-care worker to ensure that robots, sensors and devices inside our homes can function properly to take strain off healthcare systems.
This will be the person we call when our hologram doctor has difficultly beaming into our bedsides to diagnose and treat us.

6. Climate retrofitter. The world is heating up faster than we can adapt to it, so we’re going to need people to help us physically survive. This new role will plan and retrofit homes, schools and offices to be more liveable to live through hotter summers, and more frequent and intense flood and bushfire seasons. This new profession will be a sad reality of our own consequences of climate change.

7. Connection worker. As loneliness and isolation increases across all age groups, there will be professionals tasked with helping us remain connected to each other. These workers will be trained in some of the so-called “soft-skills” (that we desperately need to rename ) and will move between workplaces and communities to serve as a counterweight to the onslaught of technology.
If none of these jobs sound like you right now, that’s the point. Most new professions don’t arrive fully formed, they evolve out of small parts of existing jobs that grow over time.

Currently, for example, there’s someone in your workplace who’s setting up their first AI agent to complete work while they’re doing something else. There is someone else who is figuring out how to create stronger connections between colleagues when everyone’s in the office.

You don’t have to wait 20 years for these jobs to arrive. Look at your to-do list and identify the new tasks that didn’t exist a year ago. They might seem small today, but they are strong hints of what’s about to come.
Tim Duggan’s new book, Clear in Tension: How to get better at conflict , is out now from www.clearintension.com.au .

items.title: RBI Bulletin – November 2026
paras: Today, the Reserve Bank released the November 2026 issue of its monthly Bulletin. The Bulletin includes six speeches, four articles and current statistics. The four articles are: I. State of the Economy; II. Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict; III. Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review; and IV. Disentangling the Impact of US Monetary Policy on Indian Financial Markets: An Event Study Approach. I. State of the Economy Supply side challenges, elevated energy prices, and geopolitical uncertainty remain significant headwinds to the global economic outlook. Persistent inflationary pressures have led to synchronised monetary policy tightening across major central banks in the last three months. Pullback in AI-related stocks and elevated sovereign bond yields, despite some softening from multi-decade highs, remain a source of volatility in financial markets. Amidst uneven economic performance globally, the Indian economy stood out. High-frequency indicators of domestic economic activity showed resilience in October, underpinned by strong credit demand. Headline CPI inflation inched up, primarily driven by higher food inflation. With strong exports performance, the trade deficit narrowed in October as compared to corresponding month of the previous year. Equity markets rebounded supported by robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio inflows. Net inflows under ECB and NRI deposits also remained strong. II. Shifting Drivers of Imported Inflation: COVID-19 Pandemic to the West Asia Conflict By Snehal S. Herwadkar, Ishu Thakur, Abhiruchi Rathi, Paras and Parul Arora This article examines how successive global shocks have reshaped the drivers of imported inflation in India. It constructs an import-intensity-weighted consumer price index (CPI) using item-level production, imports and exports data to assess the contribution of imported items to retail inflation. The analysis finds that food and fuel were the principal channels through which imported inflation impacted retail inflation during the COVID-19 pandemic as also during the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Precious metals became a key source of imported core inflation from 2025, while the West Asia conflict renewed crude oil-related pressures in 2026. Highlights: The import-intensity-weighted measure indicates that imported items account for 8.5 per cent of the new CPI basket (base 2024=100). Import intensity is highest for fuel and light, followed by food and beverages, and core components. Despite the small weight of imported items in CPI basket, it contributed around 18 per cent to the CPI headline inflation in October 2026. The West Asia conflict generated a sharper crude oil price shock than the Russia-Ukraine conflict. However, the pass-through to retail fuel prices in the current episode has been relatively lower, limiting the pressures on imported inflation. Higher precious metals prices emerged as another source of imported inflation since 2024. III. Performance of the NBFC Sector during 2025-26: A Review By Monalisa Poali, Pallavi Pant, Abhyuday Harsh and Brijesh P This article assesses the performance of the non-banking financial company (NBFC) sector as at end-March 2026. Highlights: The NBFC sector continued to demonstrate double-digit y-o-y credit growth along with improvement in asset quality at end-March 2026. Industry and retail segment accounted for the largest component of NBFCs’ loan portfolio. Within retail loans, vehicle, gold and microfinance loans accounted for the largest share. Higher growth in retail loans at end-March 2026 is driven by rapid growth in advances to individuals against gold. IV. Disentangling the Impact of US Monetary Policy on Indian Financial Markets: An Event Study Approach By Mayank Gupta, Anishma Sebastian, Bhanu Pratap and Thangzason Sonna This article examines how information conveyed by the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcements is associated with Indian financial markets. It distinguishes between monetary news, which signals tighter US monetary conditions, and growth news, which reflects stronger US economic prospects. It also examines these associations across conventional and unconventional US monetary policy phases. Highlights: Increase in US G-sec yields driven by monetary news are associated with rupee depreciation, higher Indian 10-year government bond yields and lower Sensex returns. Growth news shows no statistically significant association with the Indian financial variables. The exchange rate and government bond yield are significantly associated with monetary news during both conventional and unconventional US monetary policy phases. Sensex returns are significantly associated with monetary news during the conventional phase. India VIX shows no statistically significant association with either monetary or growth news. The main findings remain broadly consistent across alternative model specifications and news-classification thresholds. The views expressed in the Bulletin articles are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1563

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

🇮🇳 sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA. The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products,… pic.twitter.com/ZlFiKOfezx

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
paras: Hello again European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment “DART made a really, really large mess. However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess.”

16 ... ... ... This image from the Hera spacecraft's asteroid framing camera shows Didymos and its smaller companion Dimorphos, revealing the stadium-sized crater created by the impact of NASA's DART spacecraft in 2022. Credit: European Space Agency This image from the Hera spacecraft's asteroid framing camera shows Didymos and its smaller companion Dimorphos, revealing the stadium-sized crater created by the impact of NASA's DART spacecraft in 2022. Credit: European Space Agency Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid’s 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

“We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess,” said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. “However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle.”

The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida . On Wednesday, ESA released Hera’s first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos . The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across.

Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there’s no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren’t sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth.

“I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid,” said Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. “In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen.”
Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable.
“As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” says Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist.

The Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid’s composition, internal structure, and mass.

Scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART’s impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos’s physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids.
“Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense,” Michel said in an interview with Ars.

In its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART’s impact showed a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos , but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera’s first images.

“As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we quickly realized the asteroids were not alone,” said Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l’Aéronautique et de l’Espace in Toulouse, France. “In fact, they had a lot of company.”

An image released by ESA on Wednesday combines 11 long exposure frames from Hera’s hyperspectral camera. Image processors on the ground digitally removed the relatively bright Didymos and Dimorphos to reveal a panoply of dimmer streaks and dots, each of which is a rock fragment ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, Murdoch said.
“Hera came to visit two asteroids, and we found hundreds of companions,” Murdoch said.

One obvious explanation for the boulders is they were thrown off Dimorphos when DART slammed into it. But scientists cautioned they need more information before they can say that with surety. Hera is the first space mission to undertake a sustained study of an asteroid with its own moon. The debris around the two asteroids might be relics from the creation of Dimorphos some time in the ancient past.

“Hera will allow us to study that in more detail,” Murdoch said. “We really need to know more about these boulders and characterize them to understand if they’re linked to DART, if they’re linked to another process, and what the consequences might be for other asteroid systems in the Solar System.”
The boulder field will create challenges for navigating around the asteroids. In particular, the boulders are an added risk for the two small CubeSats Hera is supposed to deploy in January.
“We saw a couple of images that didn’t reassure me,” said Margherita Cardi, project manager for the Milani CubeSat. “There is a mix of excitement and panic.”

Claudia Balossi, spacecraft systems engineer for Hera’s other CubeSat, named Juventas, said her mission’s planned trajectory would take it right through the boulders as it moves within a couple of miles of the asteroids, then finally toward a landing attempt on Dimorphos, where it will measure the miniature world’s tenuous gravity field.

“We are right in the middle of it,” Balossi said. “The smallest ones are probably just as big as we are and the biggest ones are very big. In the worst case, a boulder will land on us. We will activate our gravimeter right away [if that happens],” Balossi joked.

The good news is the asteroids’ gravity is so weak that Hera, Milani, Juventas, and the hazards around them all move at snail-like speeds. Hera’s current trajectory takes it around the asteroids at a relative velocity of just a quarter-mile per hour, or about 12 centimeters per second. At that speed, there’s no danger of a sudden catastrophic hypervelocity collision between the spacecraft and the boulders lurking nearby.

Scientists have seen this at an asteroid before. NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft kicked up an estimated six tons of rock and dust when it gently moved in to collect a sample from an asteroid named Bennu in 2020. Low gravity and weak surface cohesion are a recipe for outsized effects.

“These types of bodies, because of their low gravity, have a very counterintuitive behavior,” Michel said. “Each time we interact with them, whether to take a sample or to make an impact, the response of the surface was not the one we predicted, simply because our intuition relies on what we experience every day on Earth. Even if the rules of physics are the same in the Universe, they express very differently depending on local attraction.”

items.title: November 26, 1998: The day Pete Sampras secured the year-end No 1 ranking for a record sixth straight time
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to a big moment in tennis history.
On November 26, 1998, Pete Sampras set a new record by logging his sixth consecutive year-end No 1 ranking after playing a gruelling schedule post the US Open

On this day, November 26, 1998, Pete Sampras secured the year-end world No 1ranking for an unprecedented sixth consecutive time. Ironically, the news came when world No 2 Marcelo Rios pulled out during the ATP Tour World Championships, an announcement that was made on Pete’s day off. “Pistol Pete” was rewarded for his effort after he had played for six weeks without a break in order to finish the year at the top spot and break Jimmy Connors ’ record of five consecutive years as year-end world No 1.
items.impact: Sampras had triumphed four times at the US Open (1990, 1993, 1995, 1996) and twice at the Australian Open (1994, 1997), and was now only one title away from Roy Emerson’s record of 12 Grand Slam crowns.

items.title: How the ATP top 10 rankings at the end of 2026 compared to those from 2016
paras: Carlos Alcaraz secured his sixth ATP title of the year after defeating Alexander Zverev in Sunday’s ATP Finals final. The victory did little to shake up the ATP rankings – Alcaraz remains in the number three spot, behind Alexander Zverev and Jannik Sinner.

Zverev ended the season as world number one for the first time in his career, thanks in large part to the injuries suffered by Alcaraz and Sinner throughout 2026. Sinner is set to slide down the rankings in 2027, as he will be recovering from knee surgery for an extended period.

Alexander Zverev, Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Arthur Fils, Flavio Cobolli, Frances Tiafoe, Taylor Fritz and Rafael Jodar are the players included in the ATP top 10 at the end of 2026. How would you rate the 2026 WTA and ATP seasons out of 10?
items.impact: Murray won his second Wimbledon title and the Rio Olympics gold medal, while also capturing three Masters titles and finishing runner-up at the Australian Open and Roland Garros.

items.title: Comparing Mirra Andreeva’s 2026 season to what Serena Williams did at the same age
paras: Mirra Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title in 2026 and finished the year second in the world. Andreeva turned 19 this year, and became one of the best players in women’s tennis.

She will begin the 2027 season within touching distance of Elena Rybakina, the world number one. Making a significant step forward at such a young age, it’s no surprise that Andreeva has been compared to the likes of Serena Williams .

But how do they compare at the same age? Andreeva turned 19 in April 2026 and won her maiden Grand Slam title shortly after at Roland Garros. A WTA Finals triumph in November then helped her finish the season ranked second behind Rybakina. She also won titles in Adelaide and Linz and defeated five top-10 players, including Iga Swiatek and Aryna Sabalenka.
items.impact: Andreeva will have an opportunity to become the world number one in Australia next year.

items.title: Data proves why Aryna Sabalenka should not be underestimated heading into 2027
paras: The nail in the coffin of Aryna Sabalenka’s 2026 WTA campaign was administered earlier this month. Sabalenka , the former world number one, failed to advance out of her WTA Finals group for the first time since 2021, losing to Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina .

The Belarusian has struggled on the Tour since winning the coveted ‘Sunshine Double’ , suffering damaging losses to a number of lower-ranked players. Sabalenka’s woes came to a head in Indian Wells – Andreeva’s title-winning campaign in California saw Sabalenka slip to world number three for the first time since August 2024.

For all of Sabalenka’s troubles, she has much to be hopeful for heading into 2027. After such an underwhelming campaign, one could only come to the conclusion that Aryna Sabalenka’s statistical numbers have taken a hit when comparing them to the 2025 season.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
